queue.title: Managing Reputational Crisis After an Incident
queue.content:
How a company communicates a security incident often shapes reputational damage more than the incident itself. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

How a company communicates a security incident often determines the scope of reputational damage more than the incident itself.

How a company communicates a security incident often determines the scope of reputational damage more than the incident itself.

Delaying public communication about a security incident, hoping it will go unnoticed, almost always worsens perception once the information surfaces through another channel.

Clear, timely communication that acknowledges the scope of the incident and concrete recovery steps builds more trust than silence followed by a later denial.

Legal requirements to report incidents to regulators within a defined deadline are getting stricter in most jurisdictions, making delay legally, not just reputationally, risky.

A pre-prepared incident-communication protocol — templates, approval chain, designated contacts — shortens response time exactly when speed matters most.

queue.title: Digital Twins for Industrial Facilities
queue.content:
A digital twin delivers real value only with continuous sensor data, not as a one-off 3D model. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

A digital twin of a facility delivers real operational value only once sensor data updates continuously, not as a one-off 3D model.

A digital twin of a facility delivers real operational value only once sensor data updates continuously, not as a one-off 3D model.

A digital twin is not a static 3D depiction of a facility, but a dynamic model continuously updated with sensor data, enabling scenario simulation before real-world implementation.

Predictive maintenance based on a digital twin recognises equipment deviations before failure, reducing unplanned downtime that is significantly costlier than planned maintenance.

Investment in a digital twin is justified only once there's a clear operational use case — energy optimisation, predictive maintenance, or process-change simulation — not as technology for its own sake.

Integrating a digital twin with existing ERP and MES systems is often a bigger challenge than building the model itself, and deserves equal attention in project planning.

queue.title: Emergency Fund: Corporate Liquidity Reserves
queue.content:
A company without a defined liquidity reserve handles every crisis through improvisation. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

A company without a defined liquidity reserve handles every crisis through improvisation instead of a pre-prepared plan.

A company without a defined liquidity reserve handles every crisis through improvisation instead of a pre-prepared plan.

A liquidity reserve defined as a number of months of operating costs a company can cover without new revenue gives a clear, measurable framework for financial resilience.

Without a predefined reserve, every unexpected crisis — a revenue drop, a delayed large payment, a sudden cost — is handled through ad hoc borrowing on worse terms than would have been available in advance.

The size of the required reserve depends on revenue volatility and business seasonality; companies with more stable revenue can safely maintain a smaller reserve than those exposed to cyclical shocks.

Regularly testing reserve adequacy through simulated revenue-decline scenarios turns liquidity planning from a one-off decision into a continuous discipline.

Cjelovit tekst i izvor: https://gnk-asg.hr/en/publications/emergency-fund-corporate-liquidity-reserves/
